name: Ashley Moody

issue_poll.name: Mason-Dixon for NBC6/Telemundo 51 Florida Poll, 625 registered likely voters, Sept 28-Oct 1, 2026 (issue with greatest influence on 2026 vote)
issue_poll.note: Several Florida polls combined. Ranks 1-3 follow the Mason-Dixon poll, the latest with an issue question (inflation/cost of living 30, direction of state/country 17 [dropped as untestable], immigration enforcement 16, property taxes 13); its remaining options were not published in reachable text. Rank 4 from Change Research Florida poll May 13-16, 2026 (pick 3: cost of living 57, political corruption 50, property taxes 41). Ranks 5-10 from UNF PORL likely-voter poll Feb 21-Mar 2, 2026 (most important problem: affordability 50, political division 12 [dropped], immigration/education 14 among Republicans, health care 7, crime 3, environment 3, jobs 2), with housing/property insurance costs placed at 6 from Change Research cost-stress items (homeowners insurance 73%) and its top-issue rank in 2025 UNF and AIF Florida polls.

issues.detail: Strict border enforcement; faster removal of noncitizens with criminal convictions; expand state/local 287(g) enforcement
Pass Restore Trust in Congress Act: ban members, spouses, dependents from owning or trading individual stocks
Make homeownership achievable for every Florida family
Tougher penalties for violent crime; support law enforcement

plan_caveats: Moody published little forward-looking platform: no debate, no reply to the WKMG/ClickOrlando candidate questionnaire, and ashleymoody.com could not be fetched directly (seen only via news summaries).
Issue ranking stitches three Florida polls; the full Mason-Dixon and UNF toplines were unreachable, so ranks 5-10 rest on small shares (2-7%) and party subgroup figures.

Ethics rated Concrete on a bill she introduced in Jan 2026 (with Gillibrand) because Oct 2026 coverage says she campaigns on ending member stock trading; the proposal covers spouses and dependents with 90/180-day divestment.

Immigration rated Partial: forward statements are mostly 'work with Trump to reverse Biden policies'; the specifics come from bills she already sponsored (expedited removal, RIPPLE Act for 287(g)) that her campaign touts. A stricter reading would be Vague.
Crime: coverage says she pushes expanded death penalty for severe violent crimes, but the cited quote is AG-era, so only the vague direction is recorded.
Property insurance: her 2025 flood-insurance tax-deduction bill with Rick Scott is past record, not a 2026 campaign promise, so not counted.
Abortion and political division/direction of country were left out of the top 10 (abortion not in Florida issue rankings found; division/direction untestable).
